# Patterns that must never appear in this public repository.
#
# Deliberately written to match by SHAPE rather than by listing internal names:
# a pattern file that enumerates what it is hiding is itself a disclosure, and
# it hands a reader the exact vocabulary to search for. Each line below catches
# a whole family, so it also catches names that did not exist when it was
# written.

# Source paths from the private repository this code was extracted from.
src/(yotta|common)[a-z-]*/

# Internal repository names: the product word followed by a hyphen and a
# suffix. yottabot and yotta.bot are legitimate and do not match.
\byotta-[a-z]+\b

# References to internal planning and decision documents. Both name a document
# a practitioner cannot read.
#
# The first two were added after an internal planning reference reached a schema
# description published to the Terraform Registry. The ADR forms below are the
# same class and were missed by that pass: `ADR NNNN` shipped in two schema
# descriptions, and therefore in their generated Registry pages, until the
# pre-public scan caught it. When you add a pattern for one citation style,
# check for its siblings.
[Pp]lan #[0-9]
docs/plans/
ADR [0-9]{4}
\.ai/decisions

# Internal build tags and agent instruction files.
prod-[0-9a-f]{7}
CLAUDE\.md

# Cloud account identifiers, registry hosts, and resource identifiers. The
# backing cloud for a customer's deployment is an implementation detail and
# must not surface in customer-facing material.
#
# The account id is scoped to the contexts it actually appears in. A bare
# twelve-digit pattern also matches digit runs inside pinned action SHAs and Go
# pseudo-version timestamps, which made the scan fire on every workflow file.
[0-9]{12}\.dkr\.ecr
arn:[a-z-]+:[a-z0-9-]*:[a-z0-9-]*:[0-9]{12}
\.dkr\.ecr\.
amazonaws\.com

# Internal migration identifiers (bot/268, platform/060). These name a private
# repo's migration numbering and mean nothing to a public consumer, but they
# disclose the schema's change history and roughly how large it is. The repo
# carried eight of them from v0.1.0 before this pattern existed — including in
# commit messages, which the message scan below now also covers.
#
# Document the BEHAVIOUR the migration produced ("uniqueness covers live rows",
# "pinned to the server's CHECK"), never the migration's id.
\b(bot|platform)/[0-9]{2,3}\b
